pages.title: Course Detail
pages._note: A Course is a curricular container — the education 'catalog/parent' archetype. What a course owner comes here to manage is its four child collections, each its own object-list scoped by courseId: Lessons (the syllabus), Enrolments (the students taking it), Sessions & classes (the scheduled meetings), Assignments and Tests & assessments — plus the delivery Cohorts. These pair 6+6 below the metadata Data block (8-wide) and a compact Related panel (parent-course/curriculum-plan/programmes). A stats-block KPI panel counts lessons/enrolments/assignments/assessments at a glance, and lifecycleActions drives the draft→published→archived transitions (CoursePublishGuard). Course Materials render as a Files leaf — materials/handouts are the course's document surface. No email/calendar/talk: the Course schema declares NO linkedTypes and a course is a definition, not a correspondence thread (HARD RULE 1). The audit trail is a rarely-read history, so it lives as the single sidebar tab (the built-in audit widget), not a body widget (HARD RULE 4).

config._note: Board LqCursus (G2): the lessons first, then the course as a card with its figures, the other lists as tabs, sharing outside the school beside it. The outline editor (chapters with lessons, move and add inline) is an nc-vue widget still to come.

fields.text: A course only goes outside the school with an open licence, an author, open lesson material and your confirmation that it holds no learner data and the rights are settled.

pages.title: Preview as learner
pages._note: Mounts CoursePreviewView (content-adaptive-next-step-and-preview): a course author picks a simulated score and walks the course in the real lesson player in preview mode, which records nothing. Custom on purpose: it lists lessons from learniq's authors-only preview endpoint and hands off to the player, not a list or record page of one schema.

pages.title: Reissue certificates
pages._note: Mounts ReissueCertificatesView (credentials-bulk-reissue): the counts of issued, revoked and expired certificates, a required reason and the start of a queued run through learniq's own endpoint. Custom on purpose: a confirm-and-queue action against a learniq endpoint, not a list, record or dashboard of one schema.

pages.title: Course package import reports
pages._note: course-package-import-export: the anti-Canvas promise made structural — one CoursePackageImportReport per course-package import attempt, listing every source-package resource's outcome (imported/degraded/dropped). Index lists every attempt; CoursePackageImportReportDetail renders the full entries table.

pages.title: Course package import report
pages._note: course-package-import-export: renders one import attempt's full outcome — summary counts, lifecycle (running/succeeded/partial/failed), and the entries[] table (resourceIdentifier/resourceType/title/outcome/targetType/targetId/reason) naming every source resource, never a silent omission. Links to the created Course when one exists.

pages.title: Import course package
pages._note: course-package-import-export: the one genuine new custom view this change adds — uploads an IMS Common Cartridge 1.3 or Moodle backup (.mbz) package and renders the resulting CoursePackageImportReport's entries table (filterable by outcome), so an instructional designer sees every imported, degraded, and dropped resource in one place. No PHP CRUD controller — CoursePackageImportController is thin per ADR-022.

pages.title: Export course package
pages._note: Mounts ExportRequestView (learniq#947) with kind course-package: course and format, downloads from GET /api/course-management/course-package-export.

pages.title: Lesson Detail
pages._note: A Lesson is a single learning unit inside a course (ordered content item with a media contentRef) — the education content-item archetype. Body leads with lesson metadata (order, contentType, contentRef, duration, learning objectives, mandatory-training flag, regulation) 8-wide, with a Related panel resolving the parent Course alongside. Below, the lesson's Materials (files/media pointed at by lessonId) render as a related-index table plus a Files leaf, because a lesson IS its content and handouts. No comms leaves: Lesson declares no linkedTypes and is a definition, not a conversation (HARD RULE 1). Sidebar keeps metadata + an audit-trail leaf for content-change history.

pages.title: Lesson Player
pages._note: Interactive lesson playback (scene navigation, media controls, attempt tracking). No lib analogue.

pages.title: Course Builder
pages._note: course-authoring-ux: the Course/Module/Lesson tree editor — create, reorder (drag-and-drop AND keyboard move-up/move-down, WCAG 2.1 AA SC 2.1.1), and delete modules and lessons; 'Save as template' / 'New course from template' actions against the new CourseTemplate schema. No lib analogue. No new PHP controller — every write is a call against OpenRegister's existing object-create/update/delete endpoints (ADR-022).

pages.title: Lesson Composer
pages._note: course-authoring-ux: the per-lesson block editor — add/remove/reorder (drag-and-drop AND keyboard, WCAG 2.1 AA SC 2.1.1) typed content blocks (richText/media/quiz/assignment/ltiTool) and edit each block's payload, persisting the full Lesson.blocks array via OR's existing object-update endpoint. No lib analogue.

config._note: A Programme is a qualification-level container (level, code, curriculum-plan, member courses, credential template) — the education 'parent/catalog' archetype. Body leads with programme metadata (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the curriculum-plan and credential template. Below, the constituent Courses and delivery Cohorts render as related-index rosters — the two things a programme owner manages — and Final grades give an outcome roster. A stats-block KPI panel counts courses/cohorts/final-grades and lifecycleActions drives draft→published→archived (ProgrammePublishGuard). No comms leaves: Programme declares no linkedTypes and is a definition, not a correspondence thread (HARD RULE 1). The audit trail is the single sidebar tab (the built-in audit widget), not a body widget (HARD RULE 4).

pages.title: Curriculum coverage
pages._note: curriculum-coverage-matrix-view: the one custom view for reading curriculum coverage. A read-only CnDataMatrix of a framework's goals (rows, grouped under their domains) by year label (columns), each cell saying planned, assessed, both or neither, plus the gap list per subject and year. Reads the CurriculumCoverage rows curriculum-coverage-rollup keeps current; computes nothing. A menu entry next to Curriculum, deliberately NOT a Reports card (ADR-112: a report is a card or an entry, never both).

config._note: A Curriculum Plan defines the structure and pass-rules of a qualification (required/elective courses, components, formula, grade-scale, pass rules, periods) — a config/structure archetype. Body leads with the plan definition (8-wide) plus a Related panel resolving the grade-scale and owning programmes. Below, the Grade entries and Final grades computed against this plan render as related-index tables so an examinations officer can audit outcomes. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes; this is a rule definition). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail for rule-change history.

trend-and-export-reporting: columns/actionToggles declared explicitly so the platform's built-in mass import/export/copy/delete is a documented capability of this index, not an implicit default (findings 12.6/14.7).
Board LqGroep (G2): figures (lessons, enrolments, open signals), lessons today and attendance signals on the overview, the group facts and notes; teachers, work groups and the class space beside it.

pages.title: Work group
pages._note: enrolment-self-join-work-group: a teacher sets the set, name, maximum size and sign-up date, moves a learner by editing the members, and closes or reopens sign-up. Learners never read this page; they use MyWorkGroups.

pages.title: Subject teacher assignment
pages._note: A SubjectTeacherAssignment is a class x subject teacher join (cohortId, courseId, teacherId), distinct from Cohort.teacherIds — for VO/MBO/HE where a class has a different teacher per subject. Plain resource-metadata object, no lifecycle. Body leads with the assignment data 8-wide with a Related panel resolving Cohort and Course. No email/calendar/files (HARD RULE 1). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

config._note: Board LqLes (G2): presence and assignments as figures, notes and assignments on the overview, online joining, materials and the agenda beside it. The check-in code card stays the header action (SelfCheckInDialog).

content.emptyText: No notes on this lesson yet.

config._note: A Material is a learning resource (kind, file reference or URL, license, LOM tags) attached to a course/lesson/session — a document/asset archetype, so it is files-first. Body leads with the actual file/preview via a wide Files leaf, then the material metadata (kind, license, LOM tags, order) below, with a Related panel resolving the owning course/lesson/session. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail for version history.

timetabling-and-substitution: a Room is a plain bookable resource (capacity/kind/facilities/buildingCode/floor), no lifecycle — the same resource-metadata archetype as Material. Body leads with the room definition (8-wide); the Sessions booked into this room render as a wide related-index so a coordinator can see the room's schedule. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Display screen
pages._note: timetabling-display-screens: the Address action opens DisplayScreenAddress, which creates, renews or revokes the screen's secret address and shows a new address once.

pages.title: Screen address

pages.title: Optional lesson offer

pages.title: Sign-ups

pages.title: Contact hours
pages._note: timetabling-contact-hours: GET /api/reports/contact-hours behind report.contact-hours; opened from the Reports page card (category attendance).

config._note: timetabling-and-substitution: a detected (never auto-resolved) double-booking or capacity overrun. Body leads with the conflict data (kind/severity/scopeRef/detectedAt) and a Related panel resolving the referenced Sessions. Admin/coordinator/scheduling-role read only (x-property-rbac) — a learner cannot reach this page. The primary review surface is the TimetableConflictQueue custom view; this detail page is the single-object drill-down. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

timetabling-and-substitution: a learner's approved, evidence-backed exam entitlement (extra time, separate room, reader, etc.). AVG-sensitive (health/disability-adjacent) — x-property-rbac restricts read to admin/compliance-officer/mentor/the learner themselves/the submitter. Body leads with the accommodation data (accommodationKind/value/evidenceRef/approvedBy) and a Related panel resolving the linked Assessment (when set). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Timetable conflict queue
pages._note: timetabling-and-substitution: the scheduling-coordinator's review queue for open/acknowledged TimetableConflict rows (acknowledge/resolve actions). The one genuine new routed custom view this change adds — every other Room/TimetableConflict/ExamAccommodation screen is a declarative manifest page. SubstitutionModal.vue is a dialog opened from MyTimetable.vue, not a routed page.

config._note: A Rubric is a scoring scaffold (named criteria + max points) reused across assignments — a config/definition archetype. Body leads with the rubric definition including the criteria list (8-wide) and a Related panel. Below, the Assignments that reference this rubric render as a related-index so a designer sees reuse. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

An Assignment is gradable work (instructions, due date, max points, rubric, late/plagiarism policy) belonging to a course/session/cohort. Body leads with assignment details (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving course/session/rubric. The Submissions roster is the operational heart, rendered as a wide related-index, with a Submissions-received KPI stat. Briefing materials render as a Files leaf. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

A Submission is a learner's handed-in work for an assignment (attachments, feedback, rubric scores, proposed grade, linked grade entry) — a result/score record. Body leads with the submission data including feedback and rubric scores (8-wide), a proposed-grade KPI stat, and a Related panel resolving the assignment and grade entry. The submitted work renders as a Files leaf (attachments are the point of a submission). No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Submit work
pages._note: Mounts SubmitWorkView (learniq#947): CnRichSubmitDialog with the assignment's late rule; creates the Submission, attaches the files and fires submit.

pages.title: Mark submission
pages._note: Grading UI (rubric scores, inline feedback, attachments). Lib gap: grading workflow widget. peer-and-self-assessment: gains a read-only PeerFeedbackSummary/SelfAssessment context panel and, when peerReviewWeightPercent is set, an advisory-only blended-score suggestion — never pre-fills proposedGrade.

pages.title: Allocate markers
pages._note: Mounts AllocateMarkersView (assignments-double-marking): the teacher in charge names up to markersPerSubmission markers for every handed-in submission or one; learniq's POST /api/assignments/{id}/markers does the allocation. Custom on purpose: it is an action form that picks Nextcloud accounts through the core autocomplete and posts to a learniq endpoint, not a list, record or widget grid of one OpenRegister schema, so no typed page archetype fits.

config._note: A PeerReview is one reviewer's rubric-based assessment of another learner's Submission (peer-and-self-assessment) — a result/score record, mirroring Submission's own detail-page archetype. Body leads with the rubric scores + comments (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the assignment/submission. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail. x-property-rbac restricts read to admin/reviewer-self — the submission's author can never open this page directly; they read peer feedback through the PeerFeedbackSummary panel on their Submission's detail page instead.

pages.title: Complete peer review
pages._note: Reviewer's rubric-scoring UI for an assigned PeerReview (peer-and-self-assessment). Lib gap: peer-review marking workflow widget — mirrors MarkSubmissionView's own genuine-UI justification. The work under review comes from learniq's server-side projection (GET /api/peer-review/{id}/work, peer-review-projection-guard), which withholds the authors for a double-blind review and never includes the teacher's marking; the reviewer never reads the raw Submission.

config._note: A SelfAssessment is a learner's own rubric-based assessment of their own Submission (peer-and-self-assessment) — a result/score record. Body leads with the rubric scores + comments (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the assignment/submission. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail. x-property-rbac restricts read to admin/learner-self.

pages.title: Self-assessment
pages._note: Learner's rubric self-scoring UI for their own Submission, shown before-submission/after-submission/both per Assignment.selfAssessmentTiming (peer-and-self-assessment). Lib gap: self-assessment workflow widget — mirrors MarkSubmissionView's own genuine-UI justification.

config._note: PeerFeedbackSummary is a computed, read-only aggregate of a Submission's released PeerReviews (peer-and-self-assessment) — the only surface a submission's author reads peer feedback through; feedbackItems[].reviewerId is server-computed as null when the governing Assignment's peerReviewAnonymity is blind/double-blind. Mirrors FinalGrade's own read-only detail-page archetype. Body leads with the aggregate data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the submission/assignment. No lifecycle (fully derived). No comms leaves.
Board LqItembank (G2): the bank as a card and its items under it, the items as a tab too. QTI import stays a header action (lane C owns the dialog).

An Item is a single assessment question (interaction type, QTI body, correct response, max score, difficulty, subject tags). Body leads with the item definition including the QTI body (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the owning item-bank. No child rosters (an item is a leaf). No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail for revision history.
Board LqToetsInstellingen (G2): when and for whom the test is open (window, access code), the test settings, results and accommodations as tabs; course and group beside it.

config._note: An Assessment Result is one learner's attempt (responses, timing, proctoring session, grade entry). Body leads with the result data including responses (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the assessment, learner and grade entry. The proctoring evidence for this attempt renders as a related-index. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Score open answers
pages._note: learniq#948: a teacher scores one open question for every submitted attempt in turn, writing responses[].manualScore, then grades the attempts that are fully scored. No manifest page can show one question across many attempts. Reached from the results list header action.

config._note: assessment-item-pools-and-analysis: ItemStatistics is a fully-derived CTT computation (p-value, item-total correlation, distractor analysis, insufficientData gate) for one Item within one Assessment, mirroring the FinalGrade 'no lifecycle, read-only' precedent. Body leads with the statistics data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the item and assessment. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

assessment-item-pools-and-analysis: AssessmentReliability is a fully-derived Cronbach's-alpha computation for one Assessment, mirroring the FinalGrade 'no lifecycle, read-only' precedent. Body leads with the reliability data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the assessment. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Item analysis
pages._note: assessment-item-pools-and-analysis: renders ItemStatistics (p-value, item-total correlation, distractor bars) for an Item across the Assessments it appears in, and AssessmentReliability for an Assessment (via ?assessmentId= query param). No declarative chart/statistics-panel primitive exists in this register. Linked from ItemAuthorView.vue. Staff-only (RBAC enforced server-side via x-property-rbac; view also gates client-side).

config._note: A Proctoring Session records exam-monitoring for one assessment attempt (provider, status, recorded artefacts, integrity flags) — an evidence archetype. Body leads with the session data including flags (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the assessment result and learner. Recorded artefacts (video/screen captures) render as a wide Files leaf — the evidence surface. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail as a tamper log.

pages._note: Assessment-taking UI (timer, item navigation, autosave, proctoring hooks). No lib analogue.

pages._note: Mounts QtiImportView (learniq#947): uploads the package to POST /api/assessment/qti-import.

config._note: An LtiToolPlacement names which lesson/course an external LTI 1.3 tool is placed into and, optionally, which grading component its AGS scores feed — a config archetype, same shape as GradeScale. Body leads with the placement definition (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the Lesson/Course/CurriculumPlan/GradeScale it references. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes) — this is configuration, not a conversation. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail for config-change history (openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-13-lti-tool-placement/tasks.md#task-3.3).

config._note: Board LqCijfer (G2): the grade large with its weight and period, the facts of the entry and the comment for the learner; linked test, learner and group beside it. Lifecycle (publish) stays in the header actions.

governance-four-eyes: a grade in a locked report period changes only on a correction a second person approved. A teacher asks here (the grade, the new value, the reason); team leads, administration managers and admins see every request and approve or reject it on the detail page. The read rule gives a teacher their own requests only. Reached from the Grades menu and from the Ask for a correction action on a grade entry.

A correction request and its decision. Approve and reject run as lifecycle actions for the approver groups; DataCorrectionDecisionGuard refuses the person who asked. Apply is done by the app when the grade is published with the approved value. History is the audit of who asked, who approved and when it was applied.

A Final Grade is the computed outcome for a learner on a course/programme (value, passed flag, breakdown, last recompute time) — an aggregate result. Body leads with the final-grade data including the breakdown (8-wide), a value KPI stat and a passed KPI, plus a Related panel resolving learner/course/programme/plan. The contributing Grade entries render as a related-index for traceability. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Gradebook
pages._note: Mounts CohortGradebookView (learniq#947): CnDataMatrix of cohort learners by plan components; a typed mark saves a concept GradeEntry.

pages.title: Grade impact
pages._note: Grade impact detail (factor breakdown + override history). Could be type:"detail" once secondary panels lift into widgets.

config._note: course-authoring-ux: a Course Template is a reusable Course→Module→Lesson skeleton (+ optional CurriculumPlan skeleton) — a config/template archetype, mirroring LearningPlanTemplateDetail's shape. Body leads with the template definition (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the source Course (sourceCoursesId, when captured via 'Save as template'). moduleStructure/curriculumPlanSkeleton render via the generic data widget (nested arrays/objects). 'Save as template' (from CourseBuilder) creates rows here; 'New course from template' (also in CourseBuilder) reads a row and instantiates a fresh Course tree — both bespoke actions live in CourseBuilder.vue, not here. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes) — a template is a definition, not a correspondence thread. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

A Learning Plan Template defines the structure of individual learning/support plans (sections, goal domains, required signer roles, review cadence) — a config/template archetype. Body leads with the template definition (8-wide) and a Related panel. Learning plans instantiated from this template render as a related-index so a coordinator sees adoption. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

care-and-support-index: columns[] added so the care team's own read (learner, kind, coordinator, lifecycle, next review date) does not need a second index page over the same schema (ADR-097 Decision 5, ratchet gate-68 duplicate-index-pages). The CareTeamOverviewMenu nav entry deep-links here with a lifecycle=active query preset (menu[].query, the documented role-lens mechanism) rather than duplicating this page.
Board LqLeerplan (G2): goals and support measures from the record, evaluations and support requests, the OPP outflow and growth beside it when set; the plan documents as a tab.

A Learning Plan Evaluation is a periodic review of a learning plan (goal outcomes, narrative, attendees, next review date). Body leads with the evaluation data including goal outcomes and narrative (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the parent plan and attendees. Supporting documents (minutes/evidence) render as a Files leaf. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

A Signature is a cryptographic/attested sign-off on a subject object (subject kind/id/version, signer, role, assurance level, method, evidence ref) — an attestation/evidence archetype, files-first. Body leads with the signed-evidence artefact via a Files leaf, then the signature metadata (signer, role, assurance, method) and a Related panel resolving the signed subject. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail as a tamper log.

pages.title: Sign learning plan
pages._note: Mounts SignatureView (learniq#947) with subject learning-plan: CnSignatureCapture, saved as an append-only Signature.

pages.title: Learning plan editor
pages._note: Mounts LearningPlanEditorView (learniq#947): CnRelationshipGraph of the plan, goals added, reworded, reordered and removed below it.

config._note: Board LqGroepsplan (G2): the plan as a card, the group goals from the record, subgroups and evaluations as tabs, the results analysis beside it.

A GroupPlanSubgroup is a named instructieniveau split (intensief/basis/verdiept or custom) within a GroupPlan — its own differentiated goal, approach, and intended outcome. Body leads with the subgroup data (2-column) and a Related panel resolving the parent plan; the 'Learner context' KPI tile links to GroupPlanSubgroupLearnerContext.vue, the one named custom view resolving each member learner's active LearningPlan (the manifest's equality-only filter DSL cannot express the learnerIds array-membership lookup — design.md 'Why no stored link'). SupportRequests raised from this subgroup render as a standard equality-filtered object-list (originGroupPlanSubgroupId: @objectId) — no custom view needed for that reverse link. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

widgets.title: Learner context
widgets._note: The only token-resolved (@objectId) deep link from a detail page to another named route this manifest dialect supports (stats-block entry.route, resolved by CnStatsBlockWidget) — same mechanism as LearnerProfileDetail's 'Dossier timeline' KPI tile (lprof-kpis-dossier-timeline). Clicking it opens GroupPlanSubgroupLearnerContext pre-scoped to this subgroup via the subgroupId query param.

config._note: A GroupPlanEvaluation is the period-end review of a GroupPlan — a per-subgroup outcome plus an overall narrative, closing the HGW cycle. The next period's GroupPlan seeds from it via GroupPlan.supersedesId (design.md 'GroupPlanEvaluation and cycle-seeding via supersedesId'), not a forward-pointing field on this record. Body leads with the evaluation data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the parent plan. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Subgroup learner context
pages._note: groepsplan (the one genuine custom-view exception for this capability): resolves each GroupPlanSubgroup member learner's active LearningPlan (if any) — the manifest's equality-only object-list filter DSL cannot express an array-membership match against learnerIds (design.md 'Why no stored link'). Reached via GroupPlanSubgroupDetail's 'Learner context' KPI tile (gps-kpis), which resolves @objectId into this route's subgroupId query parameter — the same token-resolved deep-link mechanism as LearnerProfileDetail's 'Dossier timeline' tile (lprof-kpis-dossier-timeline). Reads subgroupId from $route.query.subgroupId. No PHP CRUD controller — reads via the OpenRegister object API only.

config._note: A SupportRequest is the zorgvraag (support/care request) raised from a pupil's dossier — the school-side start of the Wet passend onderwijs SWV chain (openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-13-zorgvraag-swv-tlv-chain). Submitting it asks integriq for an swv exchange job that hands an OSO-format dossier to the samenwerkingsverband, gated by a parent's DossierReview (data-exchange-to-integriq). Body leads with the request data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the learner and optional LearningPlan; TLV applications and deliberation records tracing to this request render as wide related-index panels. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail. Zorg data is the most sensitive category this app handles (design.md Security Considerations) — full-detail read is restricted to admin/principal plus the raising coordinator.

A TlvApplication is the toelaatbaarheidsverklaring (TLV) application tracing to a SupportRequest. Learniq RECORDS the samenwerkingsverband's decision — it never adjudicates it (design.md Decisions 'TLV decision recorded, never adjudicated'); there is no approval/rejection logic in this app. validUntil drives a declared tlvExpiringSoon calculation (no PHP TimedJob). Body leads with the application data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the SupportRequest and its linked deliberation records. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

A DeliberationRecord is a structured, append-only record of a consultation round (parents, municipality, care partners, school, SWV coordinator) concerning a SupportRequest and/or TlvApplication. Carries the pupilVoice block first — heard/statementNote or waived/waiverReason — reflecting the 2025 Wet versterking positie ouders en leerlingen in passend onderwijs hoorrecht (insight 1145); the scheduled → recorded transition is HARD-BLOCKED by PupilVoiceGuard until pupilVoice is satisfied, so the Data widget below is the coordinator's only path to clear that gate — it cannot be missed without also being unable to finalise the record. appendOnly: true once recorded — readOnly here; a correction creates a new record referencing this one (correctsId), it never mutates it. Body leads with the full record data (8-wide, pupilVoice included) and a Related panel resolving the SupportRequest/TlvApplication and attendees. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

care-and-support-index: a Trajectory tracks a bovenschoolse-voorziening placement (OPDC, rebound), referral -> preparation -> scheduled -> running -> stopped, extending SupportRequest's pattern via a nullable back-reference rather than duplicating it. Body leads with the trajectory data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the learner and optional SupportRequest; TrajectoryStatusUpdates render as a wide, append-only related-index (the status log a care team reads chronologically). No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

care-and-support-index: an append-only status-log entry on a Trajectory (ADR-008), mirroring LearningPlanEvaluation/DeliberationRecord's append-only precedent. Read-only once recorded, per the schema's appendOnly:true declaration.

care-and-support-index: structured kleuter (groep 1-2) leerlijn observation, per learner per period, mirroring IEP's documented observatie-instrument. A standing record, not a workflow (lifecycle is active/archived only). Body leads with the instrument data (entries[] renders via the generic data widget's nested-array support, 8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the learner. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes). Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

report-card-composer: a ReportPeriod is the school-wide term a periodic rapport is composed for (periodCode/academicYear/startDate/endDate/curriculumPlanIds/cohortIds/lockDate) — a config/scheduling archetype consumed by ReportCardComposer. Body leads with the period data (8-wide, includes the materialised isLocked calc) and a Related panel. lifecycleActions expose compose/archive declaratively; ReportPeriodComposeGuard blocks compose until isLocked. The richer compose confirmation (scope summary + lock-state explanation) lives in RapportvergaderingReviewView's ComposeReportPeriodModal, reached via the rapportvergadering review link. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.
trend-and-export-reporting: columns/actionToggles declared explicitly, see Cohorts' note.

report-card-composer: a ReportCard is one composed periodic rapport for one learner (subjectGrades[] snapshotting FinalGrade.breakdown.periods[periodCode], attendanceSummary, teacher/mentor comments, fail-soft docudesk PDF-render state) — a document/record archetype. Body leads with the card data (8-wide, generic 'data' widget renders subjectGrades[]/attendanceSummary as-is, no content.fields allowlist needed per the DataMappingProfile.fieldMappings precedent) and a Related panel resolving the ReportPeriod/learner. lifecycleActions expose pullIntoReview/finalise/reopen/publishToParents/recompose/renderToPdf/rerenderToPdf declaratively — ReportCardFinaliseGuard/ReportCardReopenGuard/ReportCardVisibilityGuard enforce the review-then-publish gate server-side; the cohort-wide bulk review grid lives in the separate RapportvergaderingReviewView custom view. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail. report-card-pdf-to-guardians: the card's PDF is rendered on publish and attached to the card, so card-files lists it; docudeskRenderStatus reads through its x-enum-labels in the data widget, and renderToPdf/rerenderToPdf read 'Render the PDF again' for the retry after a failed render.

report-card-templates: a ReportCardTemplate declares an ordered sections[] array (grades/lvs-results/attendance/social-emotional/narrative/pupil-voice/portfolio, each with a scale from the shared library) and a per-group testKindSectionMap[], a config/template archetype mirroring CourseTemplateDetail's shape exactly. Body leads with the template definition (8-wide, sections[]/testKindSectionMap[] render via the generic data widget's nested-array support) and a Related panel resolving the Cohorts assigned this template (Cohort.reportCardTemplateId). Assignment itself happens on CohortDetail, not here, this page only defines the template. No comms leaves (no linkedTypes): a template is a definition, not a correspondence thread. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Rapportvergadering review
pages._note: report-card-composer: the cohort-wide rapportvergadering review grid (one row per learner's ReportCard, one column per in-scope subject, inline teacherComment/mentorComment editing, finalise/reopen/publishToParents actions) — no manifest page can render a cohort grid, mirrors GradebookView's existing precedent for the same reason. Also hosts the ComposeReportPeriodModal confirmation dialog for a still-`open` ReportPeriod.

config._note: admissions-and-subject-choice: a SubjectChoice is a learner's vakkenpakket against a governing CurriculumPlan.electiveRules, gated by SubjectChoiceConsentGuard at submit and scored by SubjectChoiceValidator into validated/needs-revision. Body leads with the selection/consent/validationErrors data (8-wide) and a Related panel resolving the CurriculumPlan. lifecycleActions expose submit/revise/approve/lock as buttons. Sidebar keeps metadata + audit-trail.

pages.title: Pick electives
pages._note: admissions-and-subject-choice (task 5.3): the one genuine custom-view exception for subject choice -- an interactive elective picker for a CurriculumPlan showing live feedback against minElectives/maxElectives, mandatory combinations, and remaining capacityByCourseId before submission, which a generic manifest form cannot render. Every other SubjectChoice screen is a declarative manifest index/detail page.

pages.title: Learning
pages._note: nav-restructure-dashboards: GroupLearning's navigable landing dashboard — a bespoke domain overview with no generic index/detail/dashboard analogue. The nav icon + group association live on the GroupLearning menu entry (base manifest + this fragment's menu route), not on the page (icon/group are not valid v2 page props).

pages.title: Timetables
pages._note: timetabling-visibility-rules: look up a group's, teacher's or room's timetable within the school's visibility policy (GET /api/timetable/of). Team leads and compliance officers edit the policy here.

pages.title: Standby hours
pages._note: timetabling-standby-slots: the week's standby hours as a weekday by time grid; a coordinator adds or removes a teacher. The substitution dialog lists these teachers first.

pages.title: Hour plan
pages._note: timetabling-multi-year-hour-plan: the hours per course, year of the programme and period as a grid, with totals per year against the norm. A matrix editor the generic form cannot render.

pages.title: Teaching activities
pages._note: timetabling-multi-year-hour-plan: the teaching activities a school year needs, derived from the hour plans by GET /api/hour-plans/activities, with CSV export for the timetabling system.

pages.title: Room use
pages._note: timetabling-room-utilisation: how well rooms are used over a period, computed by GET /api/reports/room-use. Reached from a Reports card (D8), no menu entry.
